What will you build?

Describe a medical device and what it must detect. AI scientists design the smallest chip that does it.

Join waitlist Scroll, or click the monitor, to look inside

  1. The chip.

    Signals from the sensors flow in. A prediction flows out to the screen.

  2. The small fine-tuned model.

    Inside the chip runs a small AI model, fine-tuned for this one job.

  3. Wired into logic gates.

    The model is compiled into logic gates, with its weights wired in. Each gate is a handful of transistors.

  4. One chip per device.

    Every device gets its own chip: its own size, package and job. Click a chip to see what it must detect.

An AI scientist environment.

You describe a medical device and what it must detect. AI scientists take it from there and hand back the smallest chip that does the job.

  1. 1You describe a device
  2. 2AI scientists propose chip designs
  3. 3Thousands of small models fine-tune at once
  4. 4The best are compiled into logic gates
  5. 5Each circuit is checked against its model
  6. 6The smallest chip that does the job comes back

Early feasibility test

Saturday 21 November 2026, on a laptop.

2,330One small heart-rhythm detector became 2,330 logic gates

Not yet clinical. Accuracy is not yet at clinical level. This test shows the pipeline runs end to end.

Smaller, then smaller.

The AI scientists keep cutting until the chip is as small as the job allows.

  • Uses less power
  • Lasts longer on a battery
  • Costs less to make
  • Fits inside the device
